text:
Maria: ran a longctx soak with INT8 KV storage + slab allocator to reproduce the memory creep we saw earlier. details below, attaching quick logs.
Maria: setup: 8xA100, model=redwood-open-3b-int8, seq=1M tokens (simulated chat load), batch heur=adaptive, kernel-selection=auto.
Maria: observed: RSS climbs from ~6.1GB -> 9.4GB over ~200k tokens and never drops. frag_ratio reported ~0.42. reuse hit rate drops after warmup.
Maria: quick repro command: `./perf_runner --model redwood-open-3b-int8 --kv-mode slab --seq 1000000 --batch-mode adaptive --kernel auto --trace kv_alloc`
Devon: can you paste the alloc log snippet?
Maria: sure — here's the condensed output:
```
[00:02:13] KV_ALLOC slab: allocate_slab(size=32MB) -> slab_id=7
[00:02:13] KV_PAGE: page_alloc(page=2048, slab=7) -> used=2036
[00:10:02] KV_PAGE: evict_page(page=1024) -> moved to free_list (size 8k)
[00:37:11] KV_ALLOC slab: allocate_slab(size=16MB) -> slab_id=8
[00:40:00] KV_STATS frag_ratio=0.42 free_pages=312 used_pages=1296
[01:20:05] RSS 6.1GB -> 9.4GB (gradual)
```
Li-Wei: that frag_ratio is high. are we forcing page alignment for int8 blobs? int8 packing sometimes pads to 64B boundaries which increases internal waste.
Jamal: also kernel selection for int8 sometimes uses a different GEMM workspace allocation path (temp_buffer) per request, which can show up like leak if not reused across kernels.
Maria: good point — I forced kernel-selection=auto. when I pinned kernel-selection=bf16 (same model but bf16 kernels) RSS stabilized around 6.3GB. suggests kernel path triggers extra transient buffers.
Devon: do we have per-kernel workspace sizes in profiler?
Maria: yes. snippet: `kernel_workspace[int8_gemm] = 24MB`, `kernel_workspace[bf16_gemm] = 2MB`. int8 path allocs ~12–24MB per active thread and sometimes don't get returned to slab pool because of fragmentation.
Li-Wei: so two orthogonal issues: (1) int8 kernel needs larger, short-lived workspace -> pressure; (2) slab fragmentation + padding prevents reuse when workspace sizes vary.
Jamal: proposes heuristic: introduce a "slab_compact_threshold" that triggers compaction when frag_ratio > 0.30 and free_pages < N for > T seconds. simple pseudo: 
```
if frag_ratio > 0.30 && free_pages < 256 && time_since_last_compact > 60s:
    compact_kv_slab()
```
Jamal: compaction would coalesce partially filled pages into fewer slabs and return empty slabs to OS via madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) for Dedicated/private.
Maria: ran an A/B with compaction enabled (threshold=0.3, free_pages<256, cooldown=60s): RSS peak dropped to 6.7GB and frag_ratio back to 0.12 after compaction. reuse hits improved ~18%.
Devon: any quality impact from compaction+int8? did you re-run evals?
Maria: yes — re-ran the small eval set (200 prompts). INT8 perplexity delta: +0.6% on avg, top-1 token accuracy drop ~0.3%. within acceptable tradeoff for our cost targets but flagged.
Li-Wei: slight accuracy hit could be from the quantized KV pages being relocated/rounded differently after compaction? or compaction re-serializes pages with tighter packing and we lose some low-bit fidelity.
Jamal: we observed similar before: when we repack int8 KV blocks we sometimes change byte ordering for alignment which affects dequantization small amounts. suggestion: keep a copy-on-write safe repack that preserves original quantization metadata (scale/zero_point) and apply identity transform.
Maria: test results: repack-preserve-metadata reduced accuracy delta to +0.15% perplexity, top-1 drop ~0.1%. still some noise, but much better.
Devon: we should also consider a hybrid approach: keep int8 kernels but route long-lived KV pages to a dense-pool (no reallocation) and only compact short-lived pages used by kernels. avoids touching cold keys.
Li-Wei: agree. new pool concept: slabs tagged as "dense" (no compaction) vs "fragmentable" (eligible). allocator policy: assign generated KV pages from model hotness heuristics (hot keys -> dense).
Maria: implemented a PoC: hotness measured by access_count > 5 within a sliding window. results: hot pages stay in dense pool, int8 kernel workspace churn limited to fragmentable pool -- RSS stabilized and accuracy delta vanished (within noise).
ops-bot: CI:build/kv-compact-proto #782 passed (unit tests + allocator sim) :white_check_mark:
Devon: awesome. next steps? perf telemetry + rollout plan.
Jamal: open PR with: (1) slab_compact_threshold heuristic, (2) preserve-metadata repack path, (3) dense vs fragmentable slab tagging, (4) telemetry events for frag_ratio/free_pages/hotness.
Maria: I'll attach the perf traces and the small eval logs to the PR. will run longer soak (24h) before canary.
Li-Wei: also add kernel_workspace size hints into the runtime kernel selection table so we can prefer lower-workspace kernels for Dedicated longctx workloads. reduces pressure without changing quantization.
Devon: great. if soak passes, we can roll to dedicated pool next week behind a feature flag.
Maria: thanks all. saving logs to /mnt/artifacts/kvcache/soak/1823456789/ and PR from branch `kv/compact-hybrid-quant`.
